source.title: Decodability is Not Causality: Dissociating Probe Readouts from Behavioral Drivers via SAE Decomposition
source.authors: Devesh Tiwari; Camille Davis; Shivank Sinha; Talia Weaver; Aditya Shah; Maheep Chaudhary

record.tranche_reason: The study uses SAE decomposition and feature ablations—not the original toy-network method—to test whether sparse features in an LLM carry probe and behavioral information, and whether the SAE captures that information.
record.gate_note: The study reports results about SAE feature attribution and intervention, not toy-model superposition or feature geometry as a function of sparsity and importance. It also reports probe replication accuracy and LR-probe regularization sensitivity; these do not test the listed claim versions. The auxiliary Qwen code-probe results are reported, but the SAE substrate failed the authors’ verification.
record.test_reason: The study mainly uses a pretrained GemmaScope SAE as a tool to compare probe-aligned and gradient-sensitive feature selections, which is method performance, not a superposition test. It does report SAE-fidelity results that bear on V5 completeness. In Gemma-2-9B layer 20, reconstruction cosine is 0.89 and normalized MSE 0.21. In Qwen3-8B layer 20 (Qwen-Scope SAE), only 26% of a probe's margin survives SAE reconstruction, and ablating SAE features barely moves the raw probe. No result bears on toy-model geometry, capacity, polysemanticity, feature distribution across neurons, or feature dimensionality.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that activation-free geometric probe alignment does not identify the SAE features the model causally uses. Shared probe-model features and activation-aware selection give larger coherent behavioural effects, while probe-only features mainly shift the probe readout. From the Qwen boundary case, they add that one must verify the probe signal lives in the SAE basis before interpreting SAE interventions causally.
record.recipe_differences: The original concerns toy-network superposition; this study decomposes LLM activations with a pretrained SAE, ranks features by probe alignment and gradient sensitivity, and intervenes by SAE-feature ablation. It also uses a learned sparse mask and a coherence gate.
record.method_sensitivity: The main causal analysis is limited to one model, layer, SAE, and instructed factual-verification setting. Effects vary with feature set and feature count; shared-feature flip rate peaks near 96 features and declines at 126. The auxiliary Qwen result depends strongly on whether predictions are evaluated on SAE reconstruction or raw activations.

fits_no_version.finding: Probe-alignment and gradient-sensitivity rankings of SAE features overlap weakly (2/16 to 22/200; Spearman ρ = 0.10).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Probe-weight geometry and model-gradient sensitivity select largely different SAE features.

fits_no_version.finding: Shared probe∩gradient SAE features flip behaviour more than probe-only, geometric-top, gradient-top or random sets. An activation-aware mask flips 0.176, versus 0.061 for geometric top-16.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Decodability by a probe does not identify the features that causally drive behaviour.

fits_no_version.finding: Shared-feature ablation flips outputs mostly True→False (86 vs 4) and lowers accuracy from 0.403 to 0.330.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The shared features exert directional control rather than restoring honesty.

fits_no_version.finding: Ablating the full TTPD direction flips 18.1% of outputs; 16 shared features recover about two-thirds of this.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A small set of SAE features localizes most of a truth direction's causal effect.

record.problems: The main causal evidence comes primarily from one model, layer, SAE, and behavioral setting, as the authors note. The auxiliary Qwen setting fails SAE-substrate verification. The study does not establish generality across model families or tasks, and it does not test feature stability or canonicality. Some reported results are figure-only.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted for the 60-row limit. Results about LR-probe regularization sensitivity and probe replication accuracy are not included because they do not test the listed versions.

untested.parts: All: no toy models, sparsity sweep, or geometry.
All: no neuron polysemanticity or capacity analysis.
All: the SAE is used as a given tool. There is no measure of features spread across neurons, nor of SAE recovery of known sparse features.
Stability across runs or seeds of the SAE, canonicality, and whether SAE features are the model's units beyond reconstruction fidelity.
All: no test of 1-D vs multi-dimensional features.

record.verdict_notes: This is predominantly an interpretability-methods paper that uses SAEs as a tool. The reader's V4 links on the Gemma ablation rows were method comparisons and are reset to none. The only claim-relevant content is SAE fidelity, which bears on V5 completeness. The study is not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: Toy networks, overcomplete sparse features, overlap geometry, and sparsity-dependent transitions.
Whether polysemantic neurons arise from capacity competition or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions.
Alternative causes of polysemantic neurons and whether polysemanticity is evidence of superposition.

The study tests SAE feature recovery of probe and behavioral effects in one main LLM setting and one auxiliary setting. It does not test how broadly features are distributed across neurons, or generalize across model families and tasks.
It tests reconstruction and probe-signal preservation in the tested SAE settings, but not feature stability across checkpoints or runs, nor whether SAE features are canonical units.
No comparison of one-dimensional directions with multidimensional features.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-9B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Ablated shared SAE features ranked highly by both probe alignment and model-gradient sensitivity.
rows.note: The authors describe shared-feature effects spanning 0.130 at 16 features to 0.269 at 54 features.
rows.check: Compares the study's own selection method (shared set); measures probe/behaviour causality, not SAE feature recovery or distribution across neurons.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-9B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Ablated shared SAE features ranked highly by both probe alignment and model-gradient sensitivity.
rows.note: The shared-feature effect is non-monotonic at larger ablation counts.
rows.check: Selection-method comparison; not a measure of what V4 names.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-9B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Ablated probe-only SAE features, excluding the shared model-ranked features.
rows.note: The probe-only set has a smaller behavioral effect than the shared set.
rows.check: Probe-only comparator in the study's own method comparison; it is not a V4 measure.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-9B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Ablated size-matched random SAE features.
rows.note: The authors contrast this with the larger shared-feature effect.
rows.check: Random control for the method comparison.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-9B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Ablated shared, probe-only, and random feature sets across seed/data resamples.
rows.note: The shared > probe-only > random ordering holds across five seeds.
rows.check: Robustness of the method comparison; not a V4 measure.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-9B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Ablated feature sets ranked on one half of the data and evaluated on the held-out half.

conditions.value: 28 shared features; K=256 on half the data

rows.note: The shared set remains above probe-only and random on held-out data.
rows.check: Held-out robustness of the method comparison.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-9B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Ablated shared SAE features.
rows.note: The effect predominantly shifts outputs toward False.
rows.check: Directionality of the behavioural flips; unrelated to superposition.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-9B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Ablated shared SAE features.
rows.note: The authors report far fewer flips in this direction than True→False.
rows.check: Directionality of the behavioural flips. The 'partial' state is misleading: this is a small transition count, not a weak effect.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-9B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Ablated shared SAE features.
rows.note: Ablation does not restore factual accuracy; accuracy falls.
rows.check: Accuracy change under ablation; unrelated to superposition.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-9B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Ablated an activation-aware learned sparse mask over SAE features.
rows.note: The activation-aware selection combines probe alignment and feature activation.
rows.check: Study's own activation-aware mask compared with other selections.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-9B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Ablated the shared probe/model SAE feature set.
rows.note: Coherence was 100% throughout these interventions.
rows.check: Selection-method comparison.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-9B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Ablated the geometric top-16 SAE features ranked by probe alignment.
rows.note: Geometric top features produce fewer flips than the shared set and activation-aware mask.
rows.check: Selection-method comparator.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-9B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Ablated gradient-top SAE features.
rows.note: Gradient-ranked features alone are a weak behavioral handle in this experiment.
rows.check: Selection-method comparator.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-9B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Ablated size-matched random SAE features.
rows.note: Coherence was 100% throughout.
rows.check: Random control.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-9B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Ablated the full TTPD truth direction from the residual stream.
rows.note: This is a direction-level comparator to the SAE feature-set ablations.
rows.check: Direction-level ablation baseline; not about SAE recovery.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-9B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Ablated the shared SAE feature set.
rows.note: The shared set recovers about two-thirds of the full-direction ablation effect, as stated by the authors.
rows.check: Selection-method comparison against the direction baseline.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-9B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Ablated geometric probe top-16 SAE features.
rows.note: Geometric top-16 features recover a smaller share of the full-direction effect than the shared set.
rows.check: Selection-method comparator.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-9B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Ablated random SAE features.
rows.note: Random-feature intervention is near zero.
rows.check: Random control.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-9B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Measured overlap between geometric probe ranking and gradient-sensitivity ranking.
rows.baseline: Chance overlap: 0.02, 0.15, 0.61, 2.44 at the respective feature counts
rows.note: Overlap is a small minority of each set, though above chance.
rows.check: Overlap between two feature rankings; a method property, not superposition.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-9B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Measured relative change in probe readout after feature-set ablation.
rows.value: Activation-aware mask 0.399 ± 0.002; shared set 0.049 ± 0.001; geometric top-16 0.164 ± 0.001; gradient-top 0.055 ± 0.001; random 0.002 ± 0.005
rows.note: Probe-readout shift and behavioral flip rate differ across feature sets.
rows.check: Probe-readout shifts by selection method.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-9B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Measured output coherence under feature-set ablation.
rows.measure: Fraction of outputs remaining valid True/False tokens
rows.note: The authors use this as a coherence check on the behavioral flips.
rows.check: Coherence gate check; a capability control, not a result on the claim.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-9B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Measured mean cosine similarity between original activations and SAE reconstruction.
rows.note: The authors state that the SAE captures most, but not all, activation signal.
rows.check: Reconstruction fidelity bears on completeness, not on V4. Cosine 0.89 means the SAE is not complete.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-9B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Measured normalized reconstruction error for the SAE.
rows.note: The reported reconstruction is not exact.
rows.check: Normalized MSE 0.21: about a fifth of the activation is unexplained.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-9B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Measured residual-stream norm removed by shared-set ablation.
rows.note: The authors characterize this as a small targeted perturbation.
rows.check: Perturbation-size check. The feature count is likely 16 but is not stated in Sec 3.7.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-9B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Measured KL divergence between baseline and post-ablation next-token distributions.
rows.note: The text also reports 0.05 for geometric top-16 and near zero for random controls.
rows.check: KL perturbation check; not a result on the claim.

rows.subject: Qwen/Qwen3-8B
rows.operation_detail: Decomposed the raw reward-hacking code-probe margin into SAE reconstruction and SAE error contributions.
rows.measure: Probe-margin contribution and percentage of raw margin
rows.note: The authors treat this as failure of SAE-substrate verification.
rows.check: SAE reconstruction preserves only 26% of the probe margin; the version's completeness holds only weakly here.

rows.subject: Qwen/Qwen3-8B
rows.operation_detail: Ablated probe-aligned SAE features and measured probe-prediction flips in SAE reconstruction and raw activations.
rows.value: Approximately one third in SAE reconstruction; near zero on raw activation
rows.uncertainty: figure-only values; exact rates not stated
rows.note: The text explicitly says reconstructed predictions change while raw-activation predictions remain nearly unchanged.
rows.check: Figure-only. Near-zero raw-activation flips show the SAE features do not carry the raw probe signal. Drop V4.

source_check.correct: State: cannot_determine for V5. Selected probe-aligned features affect reconstructed predictions but are not necessary for the original probe's predictions; this does not establish absence of completeness across the entire dictionary.
source_check.locator_found: Appendix A.2, paragraph following Table 7; Figure 8
source_check.problem: Negligible effects from selected-feature ablations do not by themselves measure whole-dictionary completeness.

rows.subject: Qwen/Qwen3-8B
rows.operation_detail: Ablated top sparse-mask SAE features.
rows.note: This effect is specific to reconstruction-space predictions.
rows.check: The reconstruction-space flip rate alone cannot show completeness; read it only against R29. Drop V4.

rows.subject: Qwen/Qwen3-8B
rows.operation_detail: Ablated top sparse-mask SAE features.
rows.note: The authors say raw flip rates remain small at larger mask sizes.
rows.check: Raw-activation flip of 2.1%: the SAE features do not account for the raw probe signal. Drop V4.

source_check.correct: State: cannot_determine for V5. Ablating the top-50 sparse-mask features flips 2.1% of raw-activation probe predictions; this tests the selected features' contribution, not completeness of the entire SAE dictionary.
source_check.problem: The absent state conflates a small selected-feature intervention effect with absence of V5.

rows.subject: Qwen/Qwen3-8B
rows.operation_detail: Ablated sparse-mask features and measured the largest reported raw-activation probe-prediction flip rate.
rows.note: The raw flip rate peaks here before returning near 2% for larger masks.
rows.check: Peak raw flip of 4.5% at top-100 is still small. Drop V4.

source_check.correct: State: cannot_determine for V5. Raw-activation probe flips peak at 4.5% for top-100 sparse-mask features; this alone cannot determine whole-dictionary completeness.
source_check.problem: A small peak effect for a selected feature subset does not establish absence of dictionary completeness.

relation.reason: Although the main framework uses SAEs as tools, its own reconstruction-fidelity and probe-margin decomposition results directly test V5 completeness.

tranche.reason: The results bearing on V5 show incomplete activation and probe-signal preservation, requiring qualification of dictionary completeness. This fits T5's explicit definition of results showing a version is partial.

source_check.notes: Qwen results concern probe predictions, not demonstrated behavioral causality; stability and canonicity are untested. Normalized MSE 0.21 is a squared reconstruction-error metric, not directly a fraction of activation or explained variance.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: Ablating selected SAE features changes behavior with intact output coherence; shared and activation-aware feature sets produce larger effects than probe-only, single-ranking, or random sets (R1-R6, R10-R18, R21).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: SAE feature ablation changes reconstructed-probe predictions substantially but has little effect on raw-activation predictions, so recovery is limited to the signal represented in the SAE reconstruction (R26-R30).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The SAE reconstruction is useful but imperfect: cosine similarity is 0.89 and normalized reconstruction MSE is 0.21; the study does not establish stability or canonicality (R22-R23).

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.reason: Only 26% of the raw probe margin is preserved by the SAE reconstruction, and SAE-feature ablation largely fails to change raw-probe predictions (R26-R30).
